Why Is My Water Pressure Low? Causes, Tests and Fixes

By SRQ Leak Pros Editorial · Published November 5, 2026 · Updated November 5, 2026 · 8 min read

Short answer: Why is your water pressure low? If it's one fixture, a clogged aerator or valve is the usual cause. If it's the whole house, check the main shut-off, the pressure reducing valve, a leak in the service line, old galvanized pipe or work on the utility's main. Test with a hose-bib gauge. Federal building guidance suggests 60 psi or less.

Low water pressure turns a shower into a trickle and makes the washer take forever. Sometimes the fix is a five-minute cleaning. Sometimes it's a sign of a leak underground. If the cause is a leaking line, SRQ Leak Pros can connect you with a local provider for water service line repair in Sarasota.

Here's how to narrow down the cause before anyone opens a wall or the yard.

Why is my water pressure low in the whole house?

When every fixture is weak, the cause is upstream of all of them. Common causes:

  • Main shut-off partly closed. Common after a repair.
  • Failing pressure reducing valve (PRV). It can stick and choke flow.
  • Leak in the service line. Water escapes before it reaches the house.
  • Galvanized pipe. Rust builds up inside and narrows the pipe.
  • Utility work or a main break. Pressure drops for the whole street.
  • Water softener or filter. A clogged cartridge or bypass issue.
  • Peak demand. Pressure can dip when many homes use water at once.

Low pressure in one fixture only

If only one faucet or shower is weak, the problem is at that fixture.

SymptomLikely causeFix
One faucet weakClogged aeratorUnscrew and clean or replace
One shower weakClogged showerhead or flow limiterSoak in vinegar or replace
Hot water only weakWater heater valve or sedimentCheck the heater shut-off and flush
One toilet slow to fillPartly closed angle stop or fill valveOpen the valve or replace the fill valve
One bathroom weakShared branch line or valveCheck the branch valve

How to test your water pressure

A hose-bib pressure gauge costs little at a hardware store.

  1. Turn off all water use. Inside and out.
  2. Screw the gauge onto a hose bib near where the line enters the house.
  3. Open the hose bib fully and read the gauge. This is static pressure.
  4. Run a tub and read it again. A big drop points to a restriction.
  5. Test at different times. Morning and evening readings help spot utility-side dips.

The Building America Solution Center, run by the Pacific Northwest National Laboratory, recommends keeping service water pressure at or below 60 psi in the home. It notes most plumbing codes require a PRV where supply pressure exceeds 80 psi. A reading far below what you're used to points to a restriction or a leak.

Can a water leak cause low water pressure?

Yes. A leak in the service line lets water escape before it reaches your fixtures. A large leak can cut pressure sharply. A small one may barely change it but still runs up your bill. The EPA suggests a two-hour meter test. Read the meter, use no water for two hours, then read it again. If it moved, you have a leak.

Signs that low pressure comes from a leak:

  • Pressure dropped suddenly, not slowly over years
  • The meter moves with all water off
  • A wet or soft spot sits between the meter and the house
  • You hear hissing near the meter or main shut-off

When is low pressure the utility's problem?

If neighbors have low pressure too, the cause is likely the utility's main. Sarasota County's leak FAQ says customers without water are a high priority. It treats reduced pressure that stays above 20 psi as a medium priority. Report low pressure to your utility and describe what you see.

How a pressure reducing valve affects pressure

A PRV is a bell-shaped valve near where the line enters the house. It lowers high street pressure to protect pipes and fixtures. When a PRV fails, it can stick partly closed and cut flow, or fail open and let pressure spike. Many PRVs have an adjusting screw, but a failing one usually needs replacement. If your home has no PRV and you read over 80 psi, ask a plumber about adding one.

Galvanized pipe and slow pressure loss

Galvanized steel pipe has a zinc coating that wears away over decades. Rust then builds up inside the pipe and narrows it. Pressure fades slowly, often with rusty or brown water. Federal rules under 40 CFR § 141.84 even track galvanized lines that sit downstream of lead pipe. Our galvanized pipe replacement guide covers the repipe options.

Sarasota factors in low water pressure

Many Sarasota homes sit on long lots with long service lines, so a leak can hide far from the house. Older homes may still have galvanized branch lines inside walls. Neighborhoods on wells see pressure tied to the well pump and tank, not the utility. During drought restrictions, sprinkler use shifts to set hours, which can change evening pressure. If your home is on a private well, check the pressure tank and switch first.

How to keep water pressure steady

  • Clean aerators and showerheads every few months.
  • Know where your main shut-off and PRV are.
  • Test pressure once or twice a year with a gauge.
  • Watch the meter monthly for hidden leaks.
  • Replace aging galvanized or polybutylene lines before they fail.

How to increase water pressure safely

Work from the simplest fix to the hardest. Don't add a booster until you know the cause.

  1. Confirm the scope. Test two or three fixtures to see if it's one fixture or the whole house.
  2. Clean aerators and showerheads. Unscrew, rinse and soak in vinegar to clear scale.
  3. Open the main shut-off fully. A gate valve needs several full turns to open. A ball valve's handle should line up with the pipe.
  4. Check appliance screens. Washers and dishwashers have inlet screens that clog with grit.
  5. Measure with a gauge. Compare a reading at the hose bib to the PRV setting.
  6. Rule out leaks. Run the two-hour meter test before raising pressure.
  7. Adjust or replace the PRV. A plumber can set it within a safe range.
  8. Replace restricted pipe. Scaled galvanized lines won't flow well at any pressure.

Why is my water pressure low in the shower only?

Showers have extra parts that can restrict flow. Common causes:

  • A clogged showerhead or a built-in flow restrictor
  • A worn shower cartridge or mixing valve
  • A scald-guard valve set too low
  • A partly closed stop valve on the shower supply
  • Scale in the valve body from hard water

If both the tub spout and showerhead are weak, look at the valve. If only the showerhead is weak, clean or replace it.

Can a water heater cause low water pressure?

Yes, for hot water. Sediment can build up in the tank and the hot water lines. A partly closed valve on the cold inlet or the hot outlet also cuts flow. If hot water pressure is low at every fixture but cold is fine, start at the heater. Flushing the tank and checking both valves often helps. A failing dip tube or scale in a tankless heater can also cause it.

Low water pressure on a private well

Some homes in the Sarasota area use private wells. On a well, pressure comes from the pump and a pressure tank, not the utility. Common causes:

  • A pressure switch set too low or failing
  • A waterlogged pressure tank that has lost its air charge
  • A clogged sediment filter
  • A pump wearing out or a drop in the well's water level

A well pro or plumber can check the tank's air charge and the switch settings.

Should you install a booster pump?

Only after the cause is clear. A booster pump raises pressure, but it won't fix a leak, a stuck PRV or scaled pipe. It can even make a leak worse. Booster pumps fit homes where the utility supply is low for the whole street and nothing else is wrong. Ask a plumber to measure pressure and flow first.

What a plumber checks for low water pressure

CheckWhat it tells them
Static pressure at the hose bibWhether supply pressure is low or normal
Pressure while water runsWhether a restriction is choking flow
Meter with all water offWhether a leak is stealing pressure
Main valve and PRVWhether a valve is stuck or failing
Pipe materialWhether scaled pipe is the cause
Neighbors' pressureWhether the utility side is involved

Local note: older homes in Bradenton and Venice are more likely to have galvanized branch lines. Long setbacks in North Port put more buried line between the meter and the house.

When should you call a plumbing professional?

Call a pro when:

  • Pressure is low in the whole house and the main valve is fully open
  • The gauge reads above 80 psi, or far lower than it used to
  • Pressure dropped suddenly and the meter moves with water off
  • You see rusty water along with weak flow

Frequently asked questions

What is a safe household water pressure?

Federal building guidance recommends keeping it at or below 60 psi. Most plumbing codes call for a pressure reducing valve when supply pressure tops 80 psi.

Why is my water pressure low all of a sudden?

A sudden drop often points to a leak, a main break, utility work or a valve that was bumped. Check with neighbors and run a meter test.

Can a water softener cause low water pressure?

Yes. A clogged filter, resin bed or bypass valve can restrict flow. Try the bypass to compare.

Does low water pressure mean a leak?

Not always, but it can. If the meter moves with all water off, a leak is likely.

Why is my hot water pressure low but cold is fine?

The problem is likely at the water heater: a partly closed valve, sediment or a failing heater connection.
